subproblem.title: Agreement on expanding balls transfers weak convergence and boundary vanishing to the limit
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U_j ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary sets and S_j ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U_j) (j ∈ ℕ), Ŝ_j, C ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) and ρ_j ∈ ℝ with ρ_j → ∞. Assume Ŝ_j ⇀ C (WeaklyConvergesOn), Ŝ_j(ω) = currentEval(S_j, ω) for every j and every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, ρ_j), and ∂Ŝ_j(β) = 0 for every j and every β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport β ⊆ ball(0, ρ_j). Then ∂C = 0 and S_j ⇀ C in ℝ^P in the sense of ConvergesWeakly (currentEval(S_j, ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(ℝ^P)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (Us : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (Ss : (j : ℕ) → GeometricCurrentOn (Us j) (m + 1)) (Ŝ : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (ρ : ℕ → ℝ), Tendsto ρ atTop atTop → WeaklyConvergesOn Ŝ C → (∀ (j : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) ⊆ ball 0 (ρ j) → Ŝ j ω = currentEval (Ss j) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1))) → (∀ (j : ℕ) (β : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m), tsupport (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ ball 0 (ρ j) → (Ŝ j).boundary β = 0) → C.boundary = 0 ∧ ConvergesWeakly Ss C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 7 (agreement on expanding balls); cf. Simon Ch. 6, 2.13 (chapter-06.txt lines 308–313: weak convergence is convergence on each test form, and ∂ is continuous for it).
Notation: B_r := ball(0, r); 𝒟^k := TestFormOn ℝ^P k.

1. (Supports lie eventually inside the balls.) Every α ∈ 𝒟^k (any k) has compact, hence bounded, tsupport, so tsupport α ⊆ B_r for some r ∈ ℝ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball). As ρ_j → ∞, ρ_j ≥ r for all large j, and then tsupport α ⊆ B_r ⊆ B_{ρ_j}.

2. (S_j ⇀ C.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}. By step 1 and the agreement hypothesis, currentEval(S_j, ω) = Ŝ_j(ω) for all large j. Since Ŝ_j(ω) → C(ω) (WeaklyConvergesOn), the sequence (currentEval(S_j, ω))_j, which eventually coincides with it, converges to C(ω) as well (Tendsto.congr'). This is ConvergesWeakly (j ↦ S_j) C.

3. (∂C = 0.) Let β ∈ 𝒟^m. By definition of the boundary, ∂Ŝ_j(β) = Ŝ_j(dβ) and ∂C(β) = C(dβ), with dβ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1} (exteriorDerivativeTestOn); hence ∂Ŝ_j(β) → ∂C(β) (WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary). By step 1 and the vanishing hypothesis, ∂Ŝ_j(β) = 0 for all large j, so the same sequence also converges to 0. Limits in ℝ are unique, so ∂C(β) = 0. As β is arbitrary, C.boundary = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). ∎

subproblem.title: Truncation of an integer multiplicity current to a ball whose slice has finite boundary mass
subproblem.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, n := m + 1, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, S, A ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation in U (contract IMRep U n) of S (R.Represents S), with weight μ := R.measure = θHⁿ⌞M (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Let ρ, s ∈ ℝ with 0 < ρ < s and B_s := ball(0, s) ⊆ U, and assume: (i) ∂S(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) with tsupport β ⊆ B_s; (ii) A(ω) = ∫_{ball(0,ρ)} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) (Bochner integral) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U); (iii) M_{B_s}(∂A) < ∞ (SimonGMT massOn, Euclidean coefficient norm). Then there are Ŝ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and an IMRep R′ in ℝ^P such that R′ represents Ŝ (so Ŝ is integer multiplicity), R′.measure = μ⌞ball(0, ρ), Ŝ(ω) = currentEval(S, ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ ball(0, ρ), ∂Ŝ(β) = 0 for every β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport β ⊆ ball(0, ρ), and M_{ℝ^P}(∂Ŝ) ≤ M_{B_s}(∂A).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S A : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (R : IMRep U (m + 1)) (ρ s : ℝ), IsOpen U → R.Represents S → (∀ β : TestFormOn U m, tsupport (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ ball 0 s → S.boundary β = 0) → 0 < ρ → ρ < s → ball (0 : Euclid P) s ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (m + 1), A ω = ∫ x in ball (0 : Euclid P) ρ, R.orient x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) x) ∂R.measure) → A.boundary.massOn (ball 0 s) ≠ ∞ → ∃ (Ŝ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)) (R' : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), R'.Represents Ŝ ∧ R'.measure = R.measure.restrict (ball 0 ρ) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) ⊆ ball 0 ρ → Ŝ ω = currentEval S (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1))) ∧ (∀ β : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, tsupport (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) ⊆ ball 0 ρ → Ŝ.boundary β = 0) ∧ Ŝ.boundary.massOn univ ≤ A.boundary.massOn (ball 0 s)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (Simon Ch. 6, 2.9 and 3.2: the restriction T⌞B of T = τ(M, θ, ξ) to a ball is τ(M ∩ B, θ, ξ), chapter-06.txt lines 284–288 and 755–767; the bound on its boundary is the slice estimate 4.6–4.10, lines 1335–1376, which the parent supplies through hypotheses (ii)–(iii)).
Siblings: im_calculus (IMC), part (b); imrep_restriction (RS), part (c); eval_mass_bound (E1).
Notation: n := m + 1; Hⁿ := μHE[n]; M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ := R.measure; B_r := ball(0, r); ⟨α, ξ(x)⟩ := ξ(x)(α); |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; 𝒟^k(V) := TestFormOn V k (a form α belongs to 𝒟^k(V) iff it is smooth, compactly supported and tsupport α ⊆ V).

0. Preliminary facts.
 (F1) closedBall(0, ρ) ⊆ B_s ⊆ U since ρ < s; so B_ρ ⊆ U, and closedBall(0, ρ) is a compact subset of U.
 (F2) |tα| = |t|·|α| for t ∈ ℝ and every covector α: (tα)(e_I) = t·α(e_I), so Σ_I [I strictly increasing](tα)(e_I)² = t²·Σ_I [I strictly increasing]α(e_I)², and √(t²X) = |t|√X for X ≥ 0.
 (F3) If x ∉ tsupport α then α(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), hence ⟨α(x), ξ(x)⟩ = 0 by linearity of ξ(x).

1. (Restriction in U.) Apply (IMC)(b) to R and the Borel set E := B_ρ (U is open): there is an IMRep R₁ in U with carrier M ∩ B_ρ, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ (the current it represents is not needed). By (RS)(c) applied to R, E = B_ρ and R′ := R₁: R₁.measure = μ⌞B_ρ, and R₁.action(α) = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨α, ξ⟩ dμ for every n-form α (no regularity required).

2. (The same data as a representation in ℝ^P.) Let R₂ be the IMRep in ℝ^P with carrier M ∩ B_ρ, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. Its fields measurableSet_carrier, rectifiable, measurable_mult, mult_pos, aestronglyMeasurable_orient and orients only involve carrier, multiplicity, orientation and Hⁿ, so they are those of R₁; carrier ⊆ ℝ^P is trivial. Local integrability: for every compact K, (M ∩ B_ρ) ∩ K ⊆ M ∩ closedBall(0, ρ), so ∫_{(M∩B_ρ)∩K} θ dHⁿ ≤ ∫_{M∩closedBall(0,ρ)} θ dHⁿ < ∞, by monotonicity of the lower integral in the domain (lintegral_mono_set) and R.locallyIntegrable_mult for the compact set closedBall(0, ρ) ⊆ U (F1).

3. (The current Ŝ.) Apply (IMC)(b) to R₂ (domain ℝ^P, open) and E := ℝ^P: there are Ŝ ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and an IMRep R′ in ℝ^P representing Ŝ, with carrier (M ∩ B_ρ) ∩ ℝ^P = M ∩ B_ρ, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. IMRep.measure and IMRep.action depend only on carrier, multiplicity and orientation, so R′.measure = R₁.measure = μ⌞B_ρ (the second claim), and for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P):
 Ŝ(ω) = R′.action(ω) = R₁.action(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ.   (∗)

4. (Agreement.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ B_ρ. Then ω is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U (F1), so ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) and currentEval(S, ω) = S(ω) (definition of currentEval, positive branch). As R represents S, S(ω) = R.action(ω); by (RS)(c) applied to R, E = ℝ^P and R′ := R (R.carrier = R.carrier ∩ ℝ^P), R.action(ω) = ∫_{ℝ^P} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ. For x ∉ B_ρ we have x ∉ tsupport ω, so the integrand vanishes (F3), and ∫_{ℝ^P} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). By (∗) this is Ŝ(ω).

5. (No boundary inside B_ρ.) Let β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ. Then ∂Ŝ(β) = Ŝ(dβ) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply; dβ = exteriorDerivative β is a test form, exteriorDerivative_isTestForm), and tsupport dβ ⊆ tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). By step 4, Ŝ(dβ) = currentEval(S, dβ) = S(dβ), with dβ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). Also β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) (tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ ⊆ U), and S(dβ) = ∂S(β) because the exterior derivative of β ∈ 𝒟^m(U) is the same form dβ (boundary_apply). Since tsupport β ⊆ B_ρ ⊆ B_s, hypothesis (i) gives ∂S(β) = 0. Hence ∂Ŝ(β) = 0.

6. (Cut-off.) Put s′ := (ρ + s)/2, so ρ < s′ < s, and let χ : ℝ^P → ℝ be the smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius ρ and outer radius s′ (Mathlib ContDiffBump): χ is C^∞, 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on closedBall(0, ρ), tsupport χ = closedBall(0, s′) ⊆ B_s, χ has compact support, and for every x ∈ B_ρ, χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of x (ContDiffBump.eventuallyEq_one_of_mem_ball). Let β ∈ 𝒟^m(ℝ^P) with |β(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and γ(x) := χ(x)·β(x).
 (a) γ is smooth (product of smooth maps) with compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right), and tsupport γ ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ B_s ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left). Thus γ ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and tsupport γ ⊆ B_s.
 (b) |γ(x)| = χ(x)·|β(x)| ≤ 1 for every x, by (F2) and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1.
 (c) For x ∈ B_ρ, γ = β on a neighbourhood of x, so dγ(x) = dβ(x): the exterior derivative at x depends only on the germ at x (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq).

7. (Boundary mass.) With β, γ as in step 6:
 ∂Ŝ(β) = Ŝ(dβ) = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨dβ, ξ⟩ dμ   by (∗)
  = ∫_{B_ρ} ⟨dγ, ξ⟩ dμ   (the integrands agree on B_ρ by 6(c); setIntegral_congr_fun)
  = A(dγ)   (hypothesis (ii) for the test form dγ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U))
  = ∂A(γ)   (boundary_apply).
 By (E1) applied in U to the current ∂A ∈ 𝒟_m(U), the set W := B_s, the form γ and r := 1 — legitimate by (iii), 6(a) and 6(b) — |∂A(γ)| ≤ (M_{B_s}(∂A)).toReal. Hence ofReal(∂Ŝ(β)) ≤ ofReal((M_{B_s}(∂A)).toReal) = M_{B_s}(∂A), the last equality by (iii). The forms admissible for M_{ℝ^P}(∂Ŝ) are exactly such β (the support condition tsupport β ⊆ ℝ^P is vacuous), so taking the supremum (sSup_le) gives M_{ℝ^P}(∂Ŝ) ≤ M_{B_s}(∂A).

8. (Conclusion.) Ŝ and R′ satisfy all five claims: representation and weight (step 3), agreement (step 4), vanishing boundary inside B_ρ (step 5) and the boundary mass bound (step 7). ∎

subproblem.title: Sequential weak compactness of currents in ℝ^P with locally bounded mass
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n), j ∈ ℕ, satisfy sup_j M_{ball(0,R)}(T_j) < ∞ in [0, ∞] for every R ∈ ℝ (SimonGMT massOn, Euclidean coefficient norm). Then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) such that T_{φ(i)} ⇀ C, i.e. T_{φ(i)}(ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (WeaklyConvergesOn).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (T : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ R : ℝ, ⨆ j, (T j).massOn (ball (0 : Euclid P) R) < ∞) → ∃ (φ : ℕ → ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), StrictMono φ ∧ WeaklyConvergesOn (fun i => T (φ i)) C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 2.15 and the remark after Theorem 3.11 (chapter-06.txt lines 318–333 and 889–891): currents with locally bounded mass have a weakly convergent subsequence. Simon derives 2.15 from the Banach–Alaoglu theorem in the spaces M_n(W) (after representing the T_q by measures, 2.7); here, for U = ℝ^P and convergence on smooth test forms (2.13), the same conclusion is proved directly by a separability and diagonal argument, so no representation theorem is needed.
Siblings: eval_mass_bound (E1); covector_equiv (NE).
Notation: 𝒟ⁿ := TestFormOn ℝ^P n; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; B_R := ball(0, R); c_R := (sup_j M_{B_R}(T_j)).toReal ∈ [0, ∞) for R ∈ ℝ (the supremum is finite by hypothesis). By (NE) fix d ∈ ℕ and a continuous linear equivalence c from n-covectors (Mathlib's operator-norm space) onto ℝ^d with |α| = ‖c(α)‖ for all α, and let κ := ‖c‖ ≥ 0 (operator norm), so |α| ≤ κ‖α‖.

1. (Uniform evaluation bound.) If R ∈ ℝ, ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, tsupport ω ⊆ B_R and |ω(x)| ≤ r for all x, then |T_j(ω)| ≤ r·c_R for every j. Indeed M_{B_R}(T_j) ≤ sup_j M_{B_R}(T_j) < ∞, so (E1) (with U = ℝ^P, W = B_R) gives |T_j(ω)| ≤ r·(M_{B_R}(T_j)).toReal, and (M_{B_R}(T_j)).toReal ≤ c_R because toReal is monotone on finite values; r ≥ |ω(0)| ≥ 0.

2. (Test forms are bounded and supported in balls.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ. Its tsupport is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport ω ⊆ B_R for some R ∈ ℕ. The map x ↦ c(ω(x)) is continuous (ω is smooth, c continuous) with compact support (c(0) = 0), hence bounded: there is r with |ω(x)| = ‖c(ω(x))‖ ≤ r for all x. By step 1, |T_j(ω)| ≤ B_ω := r·c_R for every j.

3. (Separability.) Fix R ∈ ℕ, let 𝒯_R := {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ : tsupport ω ⊆ B_R} and K_R := closedBall(0, R) (compact). Define ι : 𝒟ⁿ → C(K_R, ℝ^d) by ι(ω)(x) := c(ω(x)). The space C(K_R, ℝ^d) is second countable (Mathlib ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology in Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.SecondCountableSpace: K_R is second countable and locally compact, ℝ^d is second countable), and on the compact domain K_R its topology is that of the sup metric dist(f, g) = sup_{x∈K_R} ‖f(x) − g(x)‖ (ContinuousMap.instMetricSpace). So it is separable, its subset ι(𝒯_R) is separable (IsSeparable.of_separableSpace), and since the space is metrizable there is a countable t ⊆ ι(𝒯_R) with ι(𝒯_R) ⊆ closure t (IsSeparable.exists_countable_dense_subset). For each g ∈ t choose ω_g ∈ 𝒯_R with ι(ω_g) = g, and let D_R := {ω_g : g ∈ t}, a countable subset of 𝒯_R.
 Claim: for every ω ∈ 𝒯_R and ε > 0 there is ω′ ∈ D_R with |ω(x) − ω′(x)| < ε for all x ∈ ℝ^P. Since ι(ω) ∈ closure t, there is g ∈ t with dist(ι(ω), g) < ε (Metric.mem_closure_iff); put ω′ := ω_g. For x ∈ K_R: |ω(x) − ω′(x)| = ‖c(ω(x)) − c(ω′(x))‖ = dist(ι(ω)(x), ι(ω′)(x)) ≤ dist(ι(ω), ι(ω′)) < ε (ContinuousMap.dist_apply_le_dist). For x ∉ K_R: x lies outside tsupport ω and tsupport ω′ (both ⊆ B_R ⊆ K_R), so ω(x) = ω′(x) = 0 and |0| = 0 < ε.

4. (Diagonal subsequence.) D := ⋃_{R∈ℕ} D_R is countable. For j ∈ ℕ put X_j(ω) := T_j(ω) (ω ∈ D), an element of ℝ^D. By step 2 every X_j lies in Π_{ω∈D}[−B_ω, B_ω], which is compact by Tychonoff's theorem (isCompact_univ_pi), and ℝ^D (product topology) is first countable because D is countable. Hence (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) there are a ∈ ℝ^D and a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with X_{φ(i)} → a, i.e. T_{φ(i)}(ω) → a(ω) for every ω ∈ D (tendsto_pi_nhds). (This is the Cantor diagonal argument.)

5. (Convergence on every test form.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ and ε > 0. Pick R ∈ ℕ with ω ∈ 𝒯_R (step 2) and put δ := ε/(4(c_R + 1)) > 0, so δ·c_R ≤ ε/4. By step 3 pick ω′ ∈ D_R ⊆ D with |ω(x) − ω′(x)| < δ for all x. The test form ω − ω′ has tsupport ⊆ tsupport ω ∪ tsupport ω′ ⊆ B_R (tsupport_sub), so by step 1 and linearity, |T_j(ω) − T_j(ω′)| = |T_j(ω − ω′)| ≤ δ·c_R ≤ ε/4 for every j. As (T_{φ(i)}(ω′))_i converges (step 4), it is Cauchy: there is N with |T_{φ(i)}(ω′) − T_{φ(i′)}(ω′)| < ε/2 for i, i′ ≥ N. By the triangle inequality |T_{φ(i)}(ω) − T_{φ(i′)}(ω)| < ε/4 + ε/2 + ε/4 = ε for i, i′ ≥ N. So (T_{φ(i)}(ω))_i is a Cauchy sequence of reals and converges (cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete); let ℓ(ω) be its limit.

6. (Linearity and bound.) By uniqueness of limits and the linearity of each T_{φ(i)}, ℓ(ω + η) = ℓ(ω) + ℓ(η) and ℓ(tω) = t·ℓ(ω); thus ℓ : 𝒟ⁿ → ℝ is ℝ-linear. Passing to the limit in step 1 (|T_{φ(i)}(ω)| → |ℓ(ω)|, le_of_tendsto'): if tsupport ω ⊆ B_R and |ω(x)| ≤ r for all x, then |ℓ(ω)| ≤ r·c_R.

7. (Continuity.) Let ω_q → 0 in 𝒟ⁿ (TestFormOnConverges): there is a compact K with tsupport ω_q ⊆ K for all q, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_q → 0 uniformly on K for every k. Choose R ∈ ℝ with K ⊆ B_R (K is bounded). For k = 0, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero) and iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 of the zero form vanishes, so sup_{x∈K} ‖ω_q(x)‖ → 0 (operator norm). Given ε > 0, let η := ε/(2(κ + 1)(c_R + 1)) > 0 and q₀ such that ‖ω_q(x)‖ < η for all x ∈ K and q ≥ q₀. Then for q ≥ q₀ and every x: if x ∈ K, |ω_q(x)| = ‖c(ω_q(x))‖ ≤ κ‖ω_q(x)‖ ≤ κη; if x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω_q, so ω_q(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). By step 6, |ℓ(ω_q)| ≤ κη·c_R ≤ η(κ + 1)(c_R + 1) = ε/2 < ε. Hence ℓ(ω_q) → 0.

8. (Conclusion.) By steps 6 and 7, ℓ together with this continuity property is a current C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn: a linear functional with the sequential continuity of step 7), and by step 5, T_{φ(i)}(ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ, i.e. WeaklyConvergesOn (i ↦ T_{φ(i)}) C, with φ strictly increasing. ∎
